text.insight: Brief text AI like a new hire: give the role, context, task, sources, limits and format.
text.detail: Tip: share the source material, give a sample to match the voice, ask for a few options, and ask “what else do you need to know?”.

words.sentenceText: Minimalist ink-wash painting: a moss-green glazed ceramic teapot set off to the right on a wooden table by a round window, steam rising. Early sun slants in; close-up, eye level; cream paper tones, vermilion accents. The words “Cloud Tea” in the left corner. Vertical 4:5 frame.

words.keywordsFor: Midjourney-style tools also take short keywords and parameters

image.insight: What you don’t describe, image AI guesses. Describe: subject, setting, style, lighting, angle, color, text, frame.

detail.text: Chat-style tools like full sentences; Midjourney-style ones also take keywords and parameters. Add reference images for consistency; fix one spot at a time, don’t rewrite.

video.insight: Each video prompt is one shot: one main action, clear camera work, plus sound and length.
video.detail: Start from an approved image to keep the product and characters right. One prompt per shot, then join the shots.

model.insight: 3D AI needs a clean photo, a clear material and purpose; the model it makes usually still needs cleanup.

detail.text: Polygons: small faces that make up an object. PBR: materials that mimic light, with color, roughness, metallic and bump maps. Blender: free 3D software.

agent.insight: Brief an agent with: the goal, when it’s done, what it may do, what to ask first, where results go.
agent.detail: An agent takes many steps on its own, so limits and check-ins to ask you matter most.

t13-mj-ar.title: Aspect Ratio
t13-mj-ar.note: Add --ar (or --aspect) after the prompt to set the aspect ratio, e.g. --ar 4:5 for a vertical frame. The docs page shows no publish date.

t13-blender.title: About Blender
t13-blender.note: Blender is free, open-source 3D software. The polygon and PBR explanations are AI Zen’s own; the need to clean up AI-made models comes from the project’s research notes (Oct 12, 2026).
